Bombyx Processionea.



Procession Moth. N. O. Lepidoptera. Tincture of live caterpillars.



Clinical. ─   Urticaria.



Characteristics. ─   Contact with the caterpillars or
        the emanations from a nest of them causes intense irritation, and hard, large, areola-formed
        tubercles, with a red areola, so thick as to leave hardly any space between. Sometimes they
        are linear-formed; most marked near joints. Sensation as if a foreign body were under the
        skin. Itching of whole body. Itching, evenings; not relieved by anything. In one victim it
        caused frequent waking at night, and dreams that his arms were being cauterised, and arrows
        thrust into the muscles. Burning heat of skin. In one case, that of a boy who shook a large
        number of the caterpillars from a tree into his naked breast, it caused an itching so severe
        that the boy had to run home for assistance; then fever, somnolency, delirium, and finally
        death ensued.



Relations. ─     Compare:
        Apis, Ast. fl., Rhus, &c.
